mintAuthority.summary: PHT's canonical Ethereum deployment mints through a Maker-style DaiJoin and Vat path. At Ethereum block 25770390, PHT Join was warded on PHT and the live Vat exposed global and USDT-A debt ceilings; the Vat ward mapping is non-enumerable, so cap administration remains a reviewed raiseable gap. The PHT token, DaiJoin, and Vat are direct immutable deployments; live wards can change mint authorization and debt ceilings but cannot replace those contracts' code. Polygon PHT and Tron PhtOFT are LayerZero bridge representations, and their owner, peer, delegate, and upgrade/configuration powers are assessed under Bridge Risk rather than global Mint Authority. No whole-supply reconciliation across the canonical token and representations is evidenced.

controls.label: APACX PHT vault/CDP mint path
controls.capDescription: PHT mints through the Maker-style Vat CDP engine. At 2026-08-16 the Vat reads Line()=250,000,000 rad (global debt ceiling), ilk USDT-A line=500,000,000 rad, and Art=6,939.383963243451574983 wad; the ward mapping is not enumerable, so the ability to change those ceilings remains unresolved.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770390 (2026-08-16): Vat 0xEE0CDe42Bb6841736d809d2Bb63EbF59dB6E336c live=1; Line()=250,000,000 rad; ilks(USDT-A).line=500,000,000 rad; Art=6,939.383963243451574983 wad. rely() simulations and wards() reads for the identified deployment-related addresses returned not-authorized/zero, but wards is a non-enumerable mapping, so those probes cannot establish that no other live ward can change the ceilings.

controls.label: DaiJoin adapter (sole warded minter on PHT ETH)
controls.capDescription: DaiJoin.exit() mints PHT permissionlessly when a user withdraws collateral-backed credit from the Vat; supply is bounded by the Vat's per-ilk debt ceilings set by Vat wards.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770390: PHT token (dai.sol fork, AGPL-3.0) wards(DaiJoin 0x4bd328fd071b03e157d0a89de199d9e005d71057)=1 (warded). DaiJoin.exit() calls dai.mint(usr, wad) permissionlessly based on Vat internal state; the live Vat is the CDP engine and its debt ceilings bound the collateral-backed path. DaiJoin.dai()=0xbe370ad45d44eb45174c4ec60b88839fef32c077 (confirmed PHT token).

controls.label: Vat CDP engine admin (debt ceiling / risk param control)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770390, rely() on the Vat reverted with 'Vat/not-authorized' from the identified deployment-related addresses and wards() reads returned zero for each. Because wards is a non-enumerable mapping, these probes do not resolve an unknown ward that could change debt ceilings or risk parameters.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770390, PHT totalSupply was 225,011,899.761301444119160709 through the reviewed Maker-style DaiJoin/Vat deployment. PHT Join 0x4bd328fd071b03e157d0a89de199d9e005d71057 was warded on PHT, and the live Vat exposed Line()=250,000,000 rad, USDT-A line=500,000,000 rad, and Art=6,939.383963243451574983 wad; the non-enumerable Vat wards mapping means the ability to raise those ceilings remains unresolved. APACX's system architecture and mint/redeem/bridge guide identify Ethereum as the primary execution environment and Polygon/Tron as LayerZero bridge representations. Their owner, peer, delegate, and upgrade/configuration powers are preserved under Bridge Risk and do not expand global native Mint Authority. No dated whole-supply collateral reconciliation across Ethereum, Polygon, and Tron was found, so reconciliation remains unknown and confidence remains manual-review. At Ethereum block 25849366 on 2026-08-27, the PHT token, DaiJoin, and Vat retained direct runtime bytecode (4,052, 1,774, and 7,006 bytes respectively), and all three contracts' EIP-1967 implementation, admin, and beacon slots were zero. The verified Maker-style sources contain no delegatecall upgrade path. Mint authorization and ceilings remain mutable through wards, as already captured by the reviewed controls, but the native contracts' mint logic itself is immutable.
